reasons: Detection is correct: Section 13/p0090 contains a Garman IP indemnity (so walk-away and 'indemnity absent/IP excluded' triggers do not apply), but it lacks the preferred-position elements — no duty to defend, no affiliate coverage, no notice/control/cooperation procedure, and no cover for Garman's breach of law, data compromise, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct. Classifying this as a deviation rather than compliant or missing is accurate.

Redline is valid and minimally invasive: it appends a single new paragraph after p0093, leaves the existing warranty indemnity and procure/modify/replace remedies untouched, and adds precisely the missing items (defence, affiliates, IP allegation trigger, breach of law, data breach, GN/WM, control-of-defence with no-adverse-settlement consent, cooperation).

The added materiality/prejudice qualifier is drafted to apply to 'any failure to give notice of a claim under this Section 13', which correctly neutralises the hard ten-calendar-day condition-precedent risk in p0090 without deleting the existing sentence.
Comment is accurate, appropriately scoped, and consistent with the paragraphs cited; tone and prefix conform.

Minor: the volunteered fallback of a 3x-annual-fees super-cap is directionally a step backwards here, since Section 15 already carves Section 13 breaches out of the liability cap entirely — recommend dropping that offer (or reserving it for later rounds) so we do not concede an uncapped indemnity unprompted.
Severity: the core IP indemnity, remedies, cap carve-out and survival are already present, so the residual gaps are important but not critical — suggest downgrading to high.
